practice.unfiltered: This guide does not use a single umbrella term such as natural or low-intervention, because no two producers mean the same thing by it and a reader has no way of checking what was meant. Instead it records four specific decisions a winemaker can state plainly and a reader can hold them to, and this is one of them. At present the producers recording it here are documented in the Adelaide Hills.
practice.unfined: This guide records four separate winemaking decisions, each stated by the producer in their own published material, rather than filing wines under a single broad label such as "natural" or "low-intervention", terms that carry no agreed definition and no way to check them. Unfined is one of those four, kept apart from the others so that a reader can see exactly which decision a given wine reflects. At present the producers documented here who state it are in the Adelaide Hills, and one such producer is published in the guide.
practice.wild_ferment: This guide records four specific cellar decisions, each one a thing a producer either did or did not do, in preference to a single loose label such as natural or low-intervention, which carries no agreed meaning and cannot be checked. Wild ferment is one of those four. The producers documented here as recording it are in the Adelaide Hills and the Yarra Valley.

region.adelaide-hills: Adelaide Hills is registered with Wine Australia as a region, and sits within the Mount Lofty Ranges zone in South Australia. The boundary takes in a long run of hill towns, among them Kersbrook, Gumeracha, Lobethal, Woodside, Hahndorf, Uraidla, Macclesfield and Meadows, and it holds two registered sub-regions of its own, Lenswood and Piccadilly Valley, either of which may appear on a label in place of the wider regional name. Across the entries published here, the varieties named are chardonnay, pinot noir, gamay, cabernet sauvignon, merlot and petit verdot.
region.yarra-valley: The Yarra Valley is registered with Wine Australia as a region, sitting within the Port Phillip zone in Victoria. Its towns run from Lilydale, Chirnside Park and Kangaroo Ground in the west through Coldstream, Yarra Glen, Gruyere and Healesville, and up into Hoddles Creek, Woori Yallock, Yarra Junction, Warburton and Toolangi, so a drive between two cellar doors carrying the same regional name can cover a good deal of ground. Chardonnay and pinot noir are the varieties named so far by published entries in this guide.

state.SA: South Australia's wine regions are registered in nineteen names, from the Riverland on the Murray and the Southern Flinders Ranges in the north, through the belt around Adelaide that takes in the Barossa Valley, Eden Valley, Clare Valley, Adelaide Plains, Adelaide Hills and McLaren Vale, out to Kangaroo Island and The Peninsulas, and down to the south-east where Coonawarra, Padthaway, Wrattonbully, Robe, Mount Benson and Mount Gambier sit. Currency Creek, Langhorne Creek and Southern Fleurieu complete the register. Of those, this guide currently documents producers in the Adelaide Hills only, and the entries published there name cabernet sauvignon, chardonnay, gamay, merlot, petit verdot and pinot noir.
state.VIC: Victoria carries twenty-one registered wine regions, from Murray Darling and Swan Hill in the north west through Rutherglen, Beechworth and the King Valley in the north east, down to Geelong, the Mornington Peninsula and Gippsland in the south, with Grampians, Henty and the Pyrenees to the west. Of those, this guide currently documents producers in one, the Yarra Valley. The varieties named in the published entries here are chardonnay and pinot noir; the rest of the state's registered ground is listed in the register but not yet covered by an entry.

subregion.piccadilly-valley: Piccadilly Valley sits inside the Adelaide Hills, in South Australia, and it is registered as a sub-region in its own right, so the name on a label marks a drawn boundary rather than a loose trade usage. Its settlements include Piccadilly, Summertown, Carey Gully and Uraidla. The published entries the guide holds for the sub-region name chardonnay, pinot noir and gamay among the fruit grown here. One producer is documented within those boundaries at present.

variety.cabernet-sauvignon: Australian labels and lists often shorten the name to Cabernet, and the two refer to the same grape. In this guide, the only region in which it is currently documented is the Adelaide Hills. That reflects which independent producers have been written up so far, not the extent of the variety's plantings, and the page will grow as further entries are published.
variety.chardonnay: Within this guide, Chardonnay appears in producer entries from two regions, the Adelaide Hills and the Yarra Valley, and three producers are published on this page so far. That reflects how far the guide's entries currently reach rather than the extent of the variety's plantings. Read the page as a record of which growers have been documented, and expect the coverage to widen as more entries are published.
variety.gamay: Australian labels use both Gamay and Gamay Noir for this variety, so a bottle carrying one name and a bottle carrying the other are the same grape. Of the regions where it is planted, the Adelaide Hills is the one this guide documents it in, through a single published entry.
variety.merlot: Within this guide, Merlot is so far documented in a single region: the Adelaide Hills, in South Australia. That reflects the makers whose entries have been published rather than the reach of the grape itself, which is planted far more widely than one region's worth of listings can show. As further entries are checked and added, other regions will appear here alongside it.
variety.petit-verdot: Within this guide, Petit Verdot is documented in one region, the Adelaide Hills, where a single published producer works with it. That is a record of which independent makers have chosen to bottle the grape under its own name and have an entry here; it is not a map of where the variety is planted in Australia, and the two should not be read as the same thing. As further entries are published, other regions may join it on this page.
variety.pinot-noir: Pinot Noir is documented in this guide in two regions: the Adelaide Hills, in South Australia, and the Yarra Valley, in Victoria. The name is frequently shortened to Pinot on labels and in trade use, so a wine listed that way may be the same grape under a shorter name. Three producers on this page currently have published entries for it, and the count moves as entries are checked and added.
